submitter: bugfix-036 thread (reviewer type slip voids whole council round) — ROUND 2, resubmit of corr 80cdd428
rationale: ROUND 2. Round 1 (corr 80cdd428) returned REVISE: 7 approve, 2 object, and the round COMPLETED without voiding (reviewers 9, abstained 7, unreadable 0). This resubmission answers every objection and carries one real code change that came out of them. NOTE FOR REVIEWERS: this code is now COMMITTED AND LIVE in the running chassis (58f5a6bb6 + round-2 ab158c32a; pod agent-chassis-5567d99bd6-5snzn greps salvageMistypedReview=2, objectionEdit=7, negative control=0). So this round is also the live verification bugs_open/036 §6 asks for — if a council_report row exists for this correlation, the class is closed, because the decider that produced it is the fixed one. ANSWERS TO ROUND 1, each checked rather than argued: (a) edit-quality e1 / constitution / prior-art-librarian asked whether rv.Missing, rv.Notes and salvaged.Degraded pre-exist, since my struct diff did not show them — they do, at diagnose_council_decide_action.go:73, :74, :79. That was my sketch abbreviating the struct, a fair hit, and the diff below now shows the whole type. (b) prior-art-librarian asked whether salvageTruncatedReview / the unreadable path / markerFieldFor are real or 019 folklore being built on — real and current: markerFieldFor:151, salvageTruncatedReview:173, unreadable appended at four call sites. (c) guardian e1 asked for confirmation that nothing downstream expects objections[].edit to be a JSON number — nothing does: no Go file outside this action and its test reads the persisted report's objections at all (fixloop_digest_action.go only COUNTS council_report rows), and MarshalJSON round-trips the original token, so a number stays a number and only a previously-fatal payload changes shape. (d) guardian e2 asked whether councilReview / councilObjection / objectionEdit are exported and consumed by another package — all three are lower-case and private to package actions, so the blast radius is the council_decide step exactly as claimed. (e) THE ONE THAT FOUND A REAL GAP, edit-quality e2, now fixed: salvageMistypedReview dropped the ENTIRE objections list when `objections` arrived as a single object rather than an array — the same wrong-register slip one level up from the `edit` field. I had asserted that was acceptable in a test (wantObjs: 0, 'the detail is lost; the opinion is not'). The seat was right that it is not: the objection list is what goes back to the proposer in a revise round, so dropping it costs the round its content even though the verdict survives. A single object is now coerced to a one-element list, with a test for the coercion and one for a genuinely uncoercible payload (objections as a string). The fix's own council caught a gap in the fix. ORIGINAL RATIONALE FOLLOWS. bugs_open/036. A council round is lost — no verdict, no council_report, no objections returned — when ONE reviewer emits well-formed JSON carrying a field in the wrong register. Live: orchestration 5438f851-db9d-4f6a-bb32-3633e6793071 died at council_decide with 'cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field .objections.edit of type int', after every seat had run and been paid for. Measured over 14 days of complete_invalid runs: 3 of 5 council_decide voids are this schema-slip cause (the other 2 are the truncation cause bugs_open/019 already fixed). All 3 named the same seat, and all 3 carried a PLAN-LEVEL description in `edit` rather than a malformed index: 'plan-level (deploy verification)', 'risks note on the 54 mis-stamped rows', 'risks/summary (item 5)'. That is the key finding and it reframes the fix: those reviewers were not emitting garbage, they were saying the objection is about the plan rather than any single edit — which the contract already spells 0. json.Number (the obvious tolerant type) would NOT have parsed any of the three. Two changes, deliberately paired. (1) Make the `edit` pointer tolerant, mapping a bare index, a numeric string, and free text (to plan-wide 0), keeping the reviewer's own token verbatim so the persisted report is not laundered. (2) The structural half: stop a single seat's malformed output from voiding the round at all. bugs_open/019 already built exactly this seam for the truncation cause — salvage the opinion, else record the seat `unreadable`, which blocks an approval downstream. This extends that SAME mechanism to cover a seat lost to a schema slip, an unserialisable payload, and an unrecognised verdict, rather than adding a second parallel degraded-round path beside it (036 §7 warns that two independently-invented degraded-round paths in one function is the split-contract drift this repo files bugs about). The safety property the old hard error protected — a council that cannot read its reviewers must not wave a plan through — is kept, but enforced where it bites: an unreadable seat downgrades approve to revise, and zero readable opinions still fails the step. So the change can only ever make an outcome more conservative, never less. Sequencing note: 036 §7 said to wait for the 019 truncation work to land before touching this file, to avoid a same-file race. It landed (11a72dc31), and the tree is clean, so the gate is cleared.

plan.summary: One reviewer's malformed output must cost one seat, never the whole council round: tolerant `edit` pointer + route schema/serialisation/verdict failures into the existing `unreadable` mechanism built for bugs_open/019.

edits.rationale: Closes both halves. The `edit` field becomes a tolerant type (objectionEdit) that never fails to parse and preserves the reviewer's own token for the report; and the three remaining return-nil-err exits in the per-seat parse loop (planBytes failure, schema mismatch on VALID JSON, unrecognised verdict) are rerouted into the `unreadable` path that bugs_open/019 already built, via a new salvageMistypedReview sibling to salvageTruncatedReview. Deliberately NOT normalising an unrecognised verdict into the nearest legal one: guessing what a seat meant is how a veto becomes an approval, so that case records the seat unreadable instead of inventing a position for it. The len(reviews)==0 fail-closed guard and the approved+unreadable downgrade are untouched — they are what keep this conservative.

Covers the two properties bugs_open/036 §6 asks a fix to prove, using the three REAL payloads from the live voided rounds rather than invented ones. Also pins a subtlety found while testing: encoding/json continues past a TYPE error (unlike a syntax error) and keeps what did decode, so a mistyped `severity` costs that field and not the objection around it — an initial expectation of 0 objections was wrong and the test now asserts the better real behaviour.
